blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and September 2026, detached houses: listings fell from 14 in June to 11 in September (−21.4%), and it took 32.4% of the city’s 37 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings fell from 16 in June to 13 in September (−18.8%), and it took 21.4% of the city’s 56 sales over the period.

items.t: No official boundary is published for the MLS name; working limits only: Hammond Road and the rail line to the north, the Fraser River to the south, the Bonson Road corridor in the middle, and the Golden Ears Business Park lands toward Harris Road to the west; exact east and west limits: UNVERIFIED.

Where the attached stock concentrates: Osprey Village and the Fraser Way / Sutton Avenue pocket at the river end of Bonson Road — and it is townhome stock, not apartment condos. The village core is Fraser Way and Barnston View Road, with the South Bonson Community Centre and Pitt Meadows Art Gallery at 10932 Barnston View Road.

SnapStats publishes medians at community level only: the Pitt Meadows condos & townhomes median was $662,500 in September 2026 ($566/sqft, 97% sale-to-list, 40 days on market), as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats GVR September 2026 report.

Transit: routes 719 and 722 run as a combined circular service through Bonson Road and Fraser Way to Meadowtown, Pitt Meadows Station and Maple Meadows Station; route 701 runs along Hammond Road at the north edge; the West Coast Express runs from Pitt Meadows Station north of the area — no station is in this sub-area.

SD42 has no middle tier (K–7 / 8–12) and catchments are address-based; the recorded locator result for 10932 Barnston View Road is Davie Jones Elementary and Pitt Meadows Secondary. Catchments for other addresses: UNVERIFIED.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in South Meadows

items.t: Rental-restriction bylaws are void — and Pitt Meadows separately prohibits short-term rentals city-wide: Since November 24, 2022 (Bill 44), no strata may enforce a long-term rental-restriction bylaw — that voids, in-entry, the Coho II directory line "rentals allowed w/restrictions" in as a restriction. The voiding does NOT create a short-term-rental right here: short-term rental accommodation is not a permitted use under the City of Pitt Meadows Zoning Bylaw — a City staff report to Council (October 23, 2024) states this expressly — and the Province's principal-residence requirement also lists Pitt Meadows.

Flood / dikes: the City's 2020 Business Plan states over 95% of the Pitt Meadows land base lies within the floodplain for the Fraser River and, to a smaller degree, the Pitt River — that current City figure governs; the guide page's "over 85%" figure is superseded and retired here. The city is almost entirely protected by 60 km of dikes, plus ditches, pump stations and flood boxes; this sub-area sits behind the Fraser River dyke in drainage Area 3 (Kennedy, including McKechnie) of the Pitt Meadows / Maple Ridge Diking District. 78% of the city's land base is in the Agricultural Land Reserve, though the urban South Bonson pocket itself is developed residential / village land.

Property taxes and drainage levy: 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, under the 2026 Annual Tax Rates Bylaw No. 3047, 2026 (adopted May 5, 2026), with a 5% penalty added after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% after August 1, 2026. The same bylaw charges a separate residential (Class 1) drainage levy of $0.1082 per $1,000 of taxable value, alongside the general municipal rate of $2.8438 per $1,000.

Suites: one secondary suite per principal dwelling unit (33 to 90 sq m, inside the same building) where the zone permits it; garden suites are one per lot at 33 to 90 sq m in the zones listed in the City garden suite guide, including RS; a lot with a garden suite cannot also have a secondary suite.

blocks.text: Good to know about South Meadows

items.t: The guide page's footer email is wrong — Jerry sweep item. The live guide page footer carries "jared@jaredgibbons.ca"; the correct address is jaredgibbons@royallepage.ca, which the page itself uses in its contact sections.

The MLS name and the City name are different places on paper. "South Meadows" exists only in the board taxonomy; the City's own name for this pocket is South Bonson. City documents, permits and the community centre all use Bonson — a buyer searching City sources for "South Meadows" will find nothing.

The floodplain figure has a stale twin on the guide page. The City's current figure is over 95% of the land base in the floodplain (2020 Business Plan); the guide page's Planning section quotes a Financial Plan figure of "over 85%", and figures around 85% still circulate. The 95% figure governs.

Two rental rules point in opposite directions here. Provincially, long-term rental caps in strata bylaws have been void since November 24, 2022 — but Pitt Meadows' zoning prohibits short-term rental accommodation outright, city-wide. A buyer underwriting either an Airbnb or a "no rentals allowed" assumption from a directory line gets both wrong.
Part of the guide page could not be read in the research pass.

The dike is the park. Shoreline Park and the dyke-top trails run on the Fraser River dike itself at 51 Bonson Road — the flood-protection structure is the neighbourhood's main recreational asset, which is why dike, drainage and the 15.0 m RS siting setback from watercourses and ditches belong in the same diligence conversation as the view.

The west edge is a business park, not future condos. The Golden Ears Business Park is being built out in phases by Onni Group in the south Bonson / south Harris Road area per City material, and the Pitt Meadows Road and Rail Improvements Project adds a four-lane underpass below the CPKC crossing at Harris Road — employment and construction context for the sub-area's west side, not residential supply.

items.t: Form B diligence (the pointer complexes are all strata): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page.

Suites and SSMUH: one secondary suite per principal dwelling unit, 33 to 90 sq m, inside the same building, where the zone permits it; garden suites are one per lot at 33 to 90 sq m in the zones listed in the City garden suite guide, and a lot with a garden suite cannot also have a secondary suite. SSMUH unit counts of 3, 4 or 6 turn on the 280 sq m lot-size threshold and the 400 m frequent-transit test; the City's OCP Amendment Bylaw No. 3034, 2025 covers 2–6 units through secondary suites, garden suites, duplexes, triplexes, townhomes and small apartment buildings.

Flood / dikes — LIVE CONFLICT flagged, retired to 95%: The guide page's Planning section states "over 85%" attributed to the City's Financial Plan 2026–2030: that is a LIVE CONFLICT with the 2020 Business Plan figure, the ~85% figure is retired here and must not be used, and no averaging is done. The city is almost entirely protected by 60 km of dikes, plus ditches, pump stations and flood boxes; this sub-area sits behind the Fraser River dyke in drainage Area 3 (Kennedy, including McKechnie), and Shoreline Park and the dyke-top trails sit on the dike itself. Confirm flood construction level, covenants and insurance for the specific complex.

ALR and airport: the City's 2020 Business Plan states 78% of Pitt Meadows land falls within the Agricultural Land Reserve citywide; the urban South Bonson pocket itself is developed residential/village land, and ALR status for a specific parcel at the sub-area's edges is a per-address ALC map check: UNVERIFIED at parcel level. Pitt Meadows Regional Airport (YPK) is west of the area across Harris Road; an official airport noise-zone map covering this sub-area is UNVERIFIED.

blocks.text: Lots and land in South Meadows
Fee-simple lots

items.t: Bonson corridor house lots: detached houses on the Bonson Road corridor and side streets under RS Large Lot Residential, R-3, R-4 and R-6 Urban Residential zones in Zoning Bylaw No. 2505, 2011, with townhome and duplex streets around Osprey Village and along Fraser Way, Bonson Road and Hammond Road.

Lot character from the zones, as stated: RS minimum lot area 0.2 ha; R-3 / R-4 / R-6 each carry a minimum lot area for subdivision of 1,215 sq m — and the 1,215 sq m figure is a subdivision minimum only and does not apply to development on existing lots, per the current bylaw text as clarified by the City's SSMUH implementation update (the newer source governing over the older bylaw reading). RM-1 Multi-Family Residential 1 (townhouse) minimum lot area 0.4 ha; RM-2 minimum lot area 3,035 sq m. Residential buildings are sited at least 15.0 m from watercourses and key or constructed ditches. These are zone figures, not a claim about any existing lot's size.

Servicing position: this sub-area sits behind the Fraser River dyke in drainage Area 3 (Kennedy, including McKechnie) of the Pitt Meadows / Maple Ridge Diking District, the urban development area serviced by ditches, culverts and storm sewers, discharging to the Alouette, Pitt and Fraser Rivers, and the City charges a separate drainage levy. A parcel-level municipal water/sewer vs well/septic statement: UNCONFIRMED in the research — confirm servicing for the specific parcel with the City.

ALR vs non-ALR: the City's 2020 Business Plan states 78% of Pitt Meadows land falls within the Agricultural Land Reserve and agriculture remains the predominant land use citywide; the urban South Bonson pocket itself is developed residential / village land, and ALR status for a specific parcel at the sub-area's edges is a per-address check on Agricultural Land Commission maps. No South Meadows-specific ALR percentage is stated.
Flood position: The city is almost entirely protected by 60 km of dikes, plus ditches, pump stations and flood boxes; Shoreline Park and the dyke-top trails sit on the Fraser River dike itself.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around South Meadows

items.t: "South Meadows" is not an official City neighbourhood name — the City describes this part of the city as "South Bonson," the Bonson Road corridor south of Hammond Road and the rail tracks to the Fraser River, including the South Bonson Community Centre at Osprey Village. No official boundary is published for the MLS name; rough working limits only: Hammond Road and the CPKC rail line to the north, the Fraser River and its shoreline parks to the south, the Bonson Road corridor in the middle, with the Golden Ears Business Park lands toward Harris Road to the west; exact east and west limits: UNVERIFIED.

Civic anchors: South Bonson Community Centre and the Pitt Meadows Art Gallery at 10932 Barnston View Road in Osprey Village; Bonson Park, 11546 Bonson Road; Pitt Meadows Athletic Park, 11431 Bonson Road, beside the Pitt Meadows Arena complex; Shoreline Park, 51 Bonson Road, on the Fraser River; dyke-top trails run along the Fraser River. The city's only library branch is in Central Meadows. Nearest hospital: Ridge Meadows Hospital, 11666 Laity Street, Maple Ridge.

Schools: SD42 (Maple Ridge–Pitt Meadows) catchments are address-based, with no middle-school tier (K–7 / 8–12). No public school building is located inside this sub-area; for the sample address 10932 Barnston View Road, the SD42 School Locator result is Davie Jones Elementary and Pitt Meadows Secondary, with French Immersion options at Pitt Meadows Elementary (Early), Eric Langton Elementary (Late) and Pitt Meadows Secondary — a completed locator run for that sample address only. Pitt Meadows Secondary, 19438 116B Avenue, is the only public secondary school in Pitt Meadows.

Market context, labelled correctly: Pitt Meadows IS a SnapStats-covered community, and SnapStats has NO land category. September 2026 context only, never land figures: South Meadows sub-area detached inventory 11 / solds 5 (45% ratio) and "Condos & Townhomes" combined 13 / 3 (23% ratio); Pitt Meadows community detached median $1,160,000 and condos & townhomes median $662,500. Sub-area medians are UNVERIFIED (community level only).

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in South Meadows

items.t: OCP — "I See Pitt Meadows 2040," Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 2864, 2020: adopted September 27, 2022, covering the whole city including the South Bonson area; it repealed the former OCP Bylaw 2352, 2007.

Zoning — Zoning Bylaw No. 2505, 2011: RS Large Lot Residential, R-3, R-4 and R-6 Urban Residential zones for house lots (minimums in), RM-1 / RM-2 for townhouse and low-density apartment sites; residential buildings sited at least 15.0 m from watercourses and key or constructed ditches. Confirm the parcel's zone in the consolidated bylaw.

SSMUH / suites as the City states it: under provincial rules applied citywide, lots 280 sq m or less allow up to 3 units, lots over 280 sq m up to 4 units, and lots over 280 sq m within 400 m of a frequent transit bus stop up to 6 units; the City's SSMUH Zoning Amendment Bylaw No. 2986 was adopted June 25, 2024, and OCP Amendment Bylaw No. 3034, 2025 covers 2–6 units through secondary suites, garden suites, duplexes, triplexes, townhomes and small apartment buildings. Suites: one secondary suite per principal dwelling unit, 33 to 90 sq m, inside the same building, where the zone permits it; garden suites are one per lot at 33 to 90 sq m in the zones listed in the City garden suite guide, including RS — and a lot with a garden suite cannot also have a secondary suite. Short-term rentals are PROHIBITED in Pitt Meadows.

Floodplain / drainage diligence: over 95% of the city is in the floodplain, behind 60 km of dikes in drainage Area 3 for this sub-area. Pitt Meadows charges a separate drainage levy inside Bylaw No. 3047, 2026 — for 2026 the residential (Class 1) drainage rate is $0.1082 per $1,000 of taxable value, alongside the general municipal rate of $2.8438 per $1,000. Budget the levy as its own line and confirm floodplain, dike and drainage details for the specific lot with the City.

ALR rules (citywide frame — 78% of Pitt Meadows is ALR; per-parcel check at this sub-area's edges): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR.

: Form B diligence (fees, amounts owed, levies, CRF balance, insurance summary; provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022 (short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw — and in Pitt Meadows STRs are PROHIBITED citywide in any event); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions. A listing's "45+" line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw.

Pitt Meadows property taxes: 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, under the 2026 Annual Tax Rates Bylaw No. 3047, 2026 (adopted May 5, 2026), with a 5% penalty added after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% after August 1, 2026. A 2026 flat utility fee amount for this area confirmed on a City source: UNVERIFIED.

blocks.text: Good to know about South Meadows

items.t: Live pages stating ~85–86% (sourced to the City Financial Plan 2026–2030) conflict with it — a genuine conflict between two City sources, flagged here for the page owner, not averaged and not silently resolved. An older City flood-mitigation release from the superseded OCP Bylaw 2352 era stated approximately 86%, which is the likely lineage of the lower figure.
A buyer searching only one label will miss stock or double-count it.

The dike is both the amenity and the diligence item: Shoreline Park (51 Bonson Road) and the dyke-top trails run on the Fraser River dike through the sub-area — dike-top trail access is part of what south-side lot buyers are actually buying, on ground that is floodplain by the City's own governing figure, with a 15.0 m siting setback from watercourses and key or constructed ditches in the RS framework.

A drainage levy hides inside the tax bylaw: Bylaw No. 3047, 2026 carries the residential drainage rate ($0.1082 per $1,000) as a separate line alongside the general rate — a carrying cost a buyer comparing headline tax rates across cities will miss.
The one page-level defect documented for this area is the floodplain conflict above.

Page-statement check for this area. Correct email is jaredgibbons@royallepage.ca. Approved page claims, where a live page states them, are the settled set only: REALTOR since 2015; 10 straight years in the FVREB Medallion Club; Top 1% of Fraser Valley Realtors; #1 in South Surrey/White Rock by MLS points for 2025 and 2026 YTD; more than $500M in sales.

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in South Meadows Pitt Meadows than in June?
faq.a: In South Meadows Pitt Meadows, listings of houses fell from 14 in June to 11 in September (−21.4%); condos and townhomes fell from 16 in June to 13 in September (−18.8%).

faq.q: How big is South Meadows Pitt Meadows compared with the rest of Pitt Meadows?
faq.a: In September 2026, South Meadows Pitt Meadows held 29.7% of the 37 houses listed in Pitt Meadows and 19.7% of the 66 condos and townhomes listed in Pitt Meadows.

faq.q: How many homes sold in South Meadows Pitt Meadows from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 12 houses and 12 condos and townhomes sold in South Meadows Pitt Meadows over those 4 months.

faq.q: How do I find out which school serves an address in South Meadows Pitt Meadows?
faq.a: School catchments are set by address, so use the school district's catchment locator with the exact address. Catchment lines change, so check before you write an offer.

faq.q: Who can help me buy or sell in South Meadows Pitt Meadows?
faq.a: Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, works across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361 or use the contact form on this site.

faq.q: Are there any apartment condos in South Meadows?
faq.a: None verified. The sub-area's 13 condos & townhomes listings in September 2026 are townhome product — Nature's Walk, Coho II, Shoreline and similar complexes around Osprey Village — and no apartment building name was confirmed on an official, developer or strata source. Buyers who need a low-rise apartment are looking at Central Meadows stock instead.

faq.q: Can I Airbnb a townhome in Osprey Village?
faq.a: No. Short-term rental accommodation is not a permitted use under the City of Pitt Meadows Zoning Bylaw — prohibited city-wide by the City layer, separate from strata bylaws — and the provincial principal-residence requirement also applies in Pitt Meadows. A strata's silence on short-term rentals does not make the use legal.

faq.q: Can I rent out a Nature's Walk or Coho II home long-term?
faq.a: Yes — strata rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022 anywhere in BC, so directory lines like Coho II's "rentals allowed w/restrictions" do not create an enforceable long-term cap. Long-term renting is the City's permitted residential use; short-term is the prohibited one — keep the two layers separate.

faq.q: What did the attached market do in September 2026?
faq.a: At the Pitt Meadows community level the condos & townhomes median was $662,500, $566/sqft, 97% sale-to-list and 40 days on market. SnapStats publishes no sub-area medians.

faq.q: Which schools serve a South Bonson address?
faq.a: No public school building sits inside the sub-area. SD42 catchments are address-based with no middle tier (elementary K–7, secondary 8–12); the locator result recorded for 10932 Barnston View Road is Davie Jones Elementary and Pitt Meadows Secondary (19438 116B Avenue, the city's only public secondary school), and Edith McDermott Elementary on Bonson Road also serves addresses to the north — check the exact address in the locator.

faq.q: Why do listings call these "South Meadows" if the count home says Mid Meadows?
faq.a: Because the MLS board label and the research geography disagree, and both bases are stated rather than smoothed over. Search both labels when comparing listings.

faq.q: Can I Airbnb an Osprey Village townhouse?
faq.a: No — short-term rentals are PROHIBITED in Pitt Meadows at the city layer; short-term rental accommodation is not a permitted use in the Zoning Bylaw.
